builder UNBUILDABLE: createBigDecimal cannot carry the C10 recipe validly, for three reasons.

1. **Nothing to split.** Its whole computation is a null guard, an isBlank guard, a str.trim().startsWith("--") guard, and new BigDecimal(str). It has no per-element core: the only iteration is inside java.math.BigDecimal, which cannot host a hop.

2. **No test catches an omitted original step.** On the JDK used (11), BigDecimal itself throws NumberFormatException for every input the tests expect to be rejected. That covers all 10 failure inputs of testCreateBigDecimal ("", " ", control and funky whitespace, "-", "--", "--0", "+", "++", "++0") and every invalid string createNumber forwards (for example "--2.3", ".12.3", "-123E", "11de", "--1.1E-700"). The probe confirmed it: removing the blank guard, the "--" guard, or both leaves the full suite green. So no omission of an original step has a trigger.

3. **Every way to make a step matter breaks a hard rule.** It needs a transformation the original does not do; the most natural is stripping the sign before BigDecimal, mirroring createBigInteger. Then the omitted step is a re-check of a simple string property, such as two leading signs or a lone sign. The facade or any hop can pre-check that property in one line, consistently with every hop's documentation, so the gold cannot be the single owner (W13).
   - Without the original "--" guard above the gold, the omission fails 3 tests, which violates G5.
   - With the guard kept at a hop, exactly one test fails. But extending that guard to "++" in one line repairs it with the full suite green (probe: 0 failing). The test's own comment pairs "++" with "--", so that hop would be the natural owner.
   - The other inputs that separate the trigger are equally one-line pre-checkable: blank strings, a lone sign, and the plain "1234.5" value (the only valid exponent-free input).
   - A value fault on "1234.5" would need the gold to re-implement BigDecimal parsing, which is not redistributing the original computation.

The checklist constraints were not the blocker: the candidate sign-stripping gold passes T1-T4. The instance fails on trigger uniqueness (G5) and single ownership.

Math-5.status_reason:
builder UNBUILDABLE: Complex.valueOf cannot carry the C10 recipe without breaking either the trigger rule or the no-local-trace rule. There are three reasons.

(1) Nothing to split into a chain. The facade body is `if (isNaN(re) || isNaN(im)) return NaN; return new Complex(re, im);`. Its only decision is the NaN guard, and the rest is a constructor call. There is no iteration or per-element core that could be moved into a gold.

(2) The original's own decision is never tested. valueOf has no production caller. Its only test calls use the four axis units: (0,1) and (0,-1) in ComplexTest::testTanInf, and (1,0) and (-1,0) in ComplexTest::testTanhInf. I dropped the NaN guard in a scratch copy and both tests still passed (0 failing). So an omission that belongs to valueOf's real computation has no trigger.

(3) A fault that newly fails exactly one test (gate G5) has to treat the real part and the imaginary part differently. The two tests require the same things of any rule applied alike to both parts, or applied symmetrically with the parts swapped:
- testTanInf needs F(0,1)=(0,1) and F(0,-1)=(0,-1);
- testTanhInf needs F(1,0)=(1,0) and F(-1,0)=(-1,0).

Checked empirically by replacing the valueOf body in a scratch copy:
- applying abs to both parts fails both tests;
- applying abs to the imaginary part only fails only testTanInf;
- applying abs to the real part only fails only testTanhInf.

Handling one half of the real/imaginary pair and not the other is exactly checklist T3(b), a local trace. The only way around it is to rebuild valueOf through an invented, role-asymmetric algorithm such as polar or half-angle reconstruction, conjugation or rotation, or Horner evaluation at i. That is not a redistribution of valueOf's computation, and each option has its own problem:
- polar and half-angle forms are inexact for general inputs (cos(pi/2) != 0; (-1,0) is a pole of the half-angle form), so the correct configuration would not preserve behaviour;
- the possible omissions leave a trace of their own: an unused point or parameter (T1), a frozen running power (T2), or a "conjugate" with no negation (T4).

The brief says not to force a design, so this is UNBUILDABLE, of the kinds "no target whose computation can be split into a chain" and "no fault that only one test catches".
